item.title: Re: Something, probably
item.content:encoded:
SCP-___J, the procrastination stone, is my all time favorite entry on the wiki and this one here reminds me of it in a very positive way. As someone who suffers a lot from impostor syndrome and low self-esteem this concept speaks to my soul. Also, please Susan come back!
If Susan also happens to work for the Foundation you could even make it a back and forth between the two of them with both (over)analyzing the same events but from different perspectives.
I mean, maybe. It might be a good idea but I'm not sure? I suppose you can figure it out by yourself anyway. Maybe if I could help here Susan would take me back…

item.title: Something, probably
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Maybe. I mean, yes, I mean…Idk man.

Page Type: Joke SCP, I think

Genre (Optional): Comedy, probably. Idk if Susan would like it.

+ Are you sure you want to open this?
- You're probably going to regret this.

Elevator Pitch: I think it's a 1979 Pontiac. Or an apple. Or a clock. Or Susan's cat. But it like, makes you doubt yourself when you talk about it. I think. Probably. I'm not sure. I'm not that good of a writer. I mean, some people say they like my writing, but Idk, you know? They could just be lying to make me feel better about myself. How am I supposed to know? Susan would know if she hadn't left me.

Central Narrative: A doctor probably tries to write the article about the object. But he keeps getting pulled into tirades about his poor life choices. I think. I mean, he might talk about why his wife left him. Or maybe he'll mention his slobbish lifestyle, and admit to eating three boxes of leftover pizza in the last week. Please come back, Susan. I love you.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: It might be unique and original? Or not. Idk. It also may provide an interesting insight into the mind of a foundation researcher? Susan might like it. And it may be a bit funny? Or not. Idk. Also, it may be a bit relatable.

Additional Notes: A few closing notes:

  • I know the article falls into the "A thing that does a thing" trope, which is why I'm going to try and have the narrative in the article focus on the mind of the researcher creating the article, and hopefully highlight some common doubts we all have in a funny way.
  • In order to keep the article coherent, I may include the more story-ish portions in addendums at the end of the article.
  • Please Susan I really miss you
